newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Fugro sees room for improvement.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Fugro sees room for improvement.

text.p: Dutch engineering consultancy Fugro NV considers a 6.0 to 6.5 percent net return on turnover achievable, chief executive Gert-Jan Kramer said on Wednesday.
Earlier, Fugro announced a jump in 1996 net profit to 35.3 million guilders, up from 15.8 million guilders in 1995 when the company was hit by bad market conditions among other factors.
The 1996 result represented a 4.3 percent net return on turnover.
Kramer told a news conference Fugro aimed to maintain a healthy balance sheet with a high cash flow to finance possible acquisitions and further technological development.
"In the offshore industry, where we have a market share of over fifty percent, there's continuous restructuring going on," he said.
He also hinted at a possible further expansion in the sector.

In January, Fugro finalised the acquisition of the survey and positioning activities of Britain's Oceonics Group Plc, which had total turnover of some five million pounds in the six months to September 1996.
"We want to obtain, maintain and enlarge our market positions, depending on the field of activity," Kramer said.

He said the offshore geotechnical services division was strongly focused on maintaining its position, while the positioning, onshore surveying and geotechnical services were aiming to acquiring market positions.
He said the new positioning services division did not make a positive contribution to results in 1996, although turnover increased more than fourfold to 17 million guilders.

"Developments are in line with the plans, but costs come before profits," he said. Kramer said a well balanced geographic spread of its activities should contribute to neutralise the effect of economic fluctuations.
In 1996, about 82 percent of turnover was generated outside the Netherlands.
North and South America together generated nearly 33 percent of turnover, Europe excluding the Netherlands accounted for 28 percent, while Asia and Australia were almost 19 percent.
Activities in the Middle East generated about two percent of Fugro's 827 million guilders turnover in 1996. Last year, turnover was up 26.5 percent compared to 1995.
Kramer also said Fugro aimed to achieve mainly organic growth.
Of the 1996 turnover growth of 173 million guilders, 67 percent was generated organically with the balance coming from currency movements and acquisitions.
Fugro more than doubled dividend to 1.50 guilders per share, implying a pay-out ratio of 49 percent.
Kramer also said Fugro's business depended far too much on short term orders and seasonal work to give a profit forecast for 1997 at this stage of the year.
